recommended_phases.title: Phase 1: Shared types — LeaveType and LeaveStatus enums
recommended_phases.rationale: Zero-dependency foundation. Every downstream module needs these enums. Single file, no logic.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2: Audit module
recommended_phases.rationale: GP-002 requires every state-changing operation to write an audit record. Audit is a cross-cutting dependency for balance and leave. Depends only on shared-types.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3: Employee module
recommended_phases.rationale: Leave service needs employee lookup and manager-subordinate validation. Depends only on shared-types.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4: Policy module
recommended_phases.rationale: LeavePolicy defines allowances per leave type and fiscal year. Balance initialization and leave validation both depend on policy. Depends only on shared-types.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 5: Balance module
recommended_phases.rationale: LeaveBalance tracks per-employee, per-type, per-fiscal-year balances. Depends on policy (for default allowances), audit (GP-002), and shared-types.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 6: Notification module
recommended_phases.rationale: Lightweight module for notifying employees and managers on leave events. Depends only on shared-types.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 7: Leave model and repository
recommended_phases.rationale: LeaveRequest model and its repository layer. Depends on shared-types for LeaveType and LeaveStatus enums.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 8: Leave service
recommended_phases.rationale: Core business logic: submit, approve, reject, cancel. Orchestrates balance, policy, employee, notification, and audit. Depends on all prior modules.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 9: Leave controller and routes
recommended_phases.rationale: Fastify route handlers with RBAC guards and input validation. Exposes the REST API surface for the leave module.

app_notes: Layer boundaries: presentation (controller + routes) → application (services) → domain (models + repository interfaces) → infrastructure (repository implementations, db connection). Dependencies flow inward. LeaveService is the central orchestrator: submitRequest validates against policy, checks balance, deducts, creates the request, audits, and notifies. approveRequest/rejectRequest validate manager authority via EmployeeService, update status, adjust balance if needed, audit, and notify. All state-changing operations go through repositories and produce audit records (GP-002). RBAC is enforced at the route level via a requireRole guard (GP-005). Input validation happens at the controller boundary (GP-003). The balance deduction timing is left as an open question — the current interface supports single-phase deductBalance but the open question captures the two-phase alternatives.

open_questions.question: When should leave balance be deducted — on submission (reserve/hold) or on approval (finalize)?
open_questions.impact: Determines whether BalanceService needs both `holdBalance` and `deductBalance` (two-phase) or just `deductBalance` (single-phase). Affects the submitRequest and approveRequest/rejectRequest flows in LeaveService, and the restore/cancel semantics.
candidate_options: Deduct on submission with restore on rejection/cancellation (reserve model)
Two-phase: hold on submission, commit on approval, release on rejection

auth_contract: request.user: { id: string; role: UserRole } where UserRole = 'employee' | 'manager' | 'hr_admin'. JWT bearer token verified by an auth middleware (fastify hook) that populates request.user. RBAC enforced by a requireRole(...roles) route-level guard, never inline in handlers.
error_response_contract: Standard error shape: { error: string; code: string }. Validation failure → HTTP 400. Authentication failure → 401. Authorization failure → 403. Not found → 404. Internal server error → 500.
